title: AkashicNET Global Metadata Discovery Seed
boundaries: Presence in a source does not establish truth.
Documentary trace is not the same as ultimate origin.
Unknown is a valid value and must not be silently replaced by speculation.
Connections are discovery paths, not causal claims or corroboration.
Living people, private data and restricted archives are excluded by default.
Indigenous knowledge requires consent, context and cultural-sovereignty review.

topics.label: Quality of life
topics.summary: How people experience their lives across health, autonomy, relationships, meaning, environment, material security and opportunity.

origin.documentary_trace: Longstanding human concern; modern cross-cultural measurement includes the WHOQOL programme developed through fifteen international field centres.
origin.evidence_note: Quality of life is multidimensional and value-sensitive. No single index captures every person, culture or circumstance.

rights.note: Only original summaries and links are included. Instrument, dataset and document reuse conditions require item-level review.

open_questions: Which dimensions matter most to people in different cultures and circumstances?
How should subjective experience and objective living conditions be combined without erasing either?
Which interventions improve several dimensions without shifting harms onto other people, future generations or ecosystems?
How can minority needs and neurodivergent lives remain visible in population averages?

candidates.label: Secure basic needs and accessible essential services
Strengthen social connection and community participation
Support sleep, movement, nutrition and preventive care
Design work, technology and public space for autonomy and accessibility
Protect ecological conditions that sustain present and future lives
Make room for meaning, contemplation, creativity and service
tradeoffs: cannot replace clinical or material support

review.notes: Worked pilot generated from public institutional metadata; synthesis and solution ratings require independent review before public promotion.
